about: Film directions for scripts/deck.py. Each entry is a complete art direction for a 6-45 s launch or product film, or an 8-20 s update film: its world and light, camera, cuts, type, story shape, one signature shot, the lockup, a beat skeleton and music. deck.py deals three that fit the brief; the agent chooses the one that carries the subject's idea, then the full sheet is dealt. Edit this file, then run `python3 scripts/deck.py --validate`.

floor.about: The floor against a flat film, checked on renders: the picture never rests.

defaults.foreground: a pre-softened near plane made of the product's own things: a real card, chip, tile or mark from the film, in its own colours and with its content, legible as itself, 1.2-1.6x the frame height, softened once in its plate (never an animated blur), crossing or drifting at 1.5-2.5x the camera's speed near a frame edge, so every shot has a near, a middle and a far plane. Never a blank or dark-toned shape at low opacity: every element in frame has a job, and a faint plate with nothing on it is filler; a direction turns it off only with a reason

ground_families.about: One field and its light for the whole film (references/brand-and-color.md §9b; fx/Grounds FamilyGround draws it, palette.py --family writes its tokens). deck.py deals one per sheet, weighted toward the dealt palette's tone and never the family of the last three films; the ground never cuts and its one colour event is declared. The bans stay.

methods.relief: Extruded solids on a floor under one key, drawn as one SVG per frame (no CSS 3D, no filters on the blocks). Each block is a footprint polygon and a height h in px at 1080p. Project its corners every frame with one perspective function written once for the film (camera position, pitch and focal length as functions of the frame), then frame the result with the shot (toScreen or camera()): the top face is the footprint lifted by h; draw only the side faces whose outward normal faces the camera (at most two for a box). Paint back to front, sorted by the depth of each footprint's centre. Face fills come from the face-shade method. Cast shadows: for a key at elevation e and azimuth a, a block's shadow is the convex hull of its footprint and the footprint moved h x cot(e) along a; all shadows go into ONE path inside a group at opacity 0.14-0.24, so overlapping shadows never darken twice; shadows are drawn after the floor and before the blocks. A constant 1.5 px blur on that one group gives a penumbra (never an animated blur radius). Budget: 400 blocks of three polygons plus the shadow path is about 1,200 SVG nodes, fine at 1080p60.
methods.face-shade: Matte faces lit by one fixed key. For each face, n.l is the cosine between its current normal and the key direction; its shade overlay (a div or SVG polygon in ink over the face) has opacity k x (1 - (a + (1 - a) x max(0, n.l))) with ambient a 0.55-0.70 and k 0.5-0.8, so a face turned fully away sits 0.12-0.22 L below one facing the key. Matte only: no specular band, no moving highlight. Solids have real faces (backface-visibility hidden on a preserve-3d box of true thickness), never a stack of thin layers faking an edge.
methods.plate-light: The house light field built from plain parts: one or two baked, dithered one-hue plates (made once with the dither script, scripts/dither-*.py, at half size and scaled up) moved by transform and opacity only. Light is motivated and subtle: a key falloff from one side (a lightness swing of 0.02-0.10 behind content), or a pool only where the place has a lamp, a window or a lit object, travelling at 180-300 px/s; never a lit patch behind a line, a lockup or a card, and never a white haze over the frame. A reveal lifts the key plate x2 over 0.9 s. Chroma 0.13 or less, accent hue only. Never animated CSS colour ramps.
methods.exposure-plate: An exposure event from plain parts: the arriving element's own plate one step lighter (or the frame through CSS filter brightness() on the scene root within 0.94-1.08), opacity 0 -> peak -> 0 over 0.5-0.9 s on softOut (peak 0.06-0.12 for a lift, 0.15-0.25 for a dip); a full-frame veil of the lighter step only on a declared light seam, never held. At least one per act; never a dip to black, never a white haze that stays.
methods.tile-field: Many identical elements driven by one front: N absolutely positioned elements (divs, or SVG above 400), each with a fixed slot. A front is a function d(i): distance from an origin, a diagonal col + row, or a rank. Element i starts at t0 + d(i) x stagger and runs one fixed curve over D frames, closed form in the frame; no element reads another's state. Elements under 12 px on screen drop their shadow and inner detail.
methods.projection: A point light throws silhouettes on a wall. An object at distance z from the light, with the wall at distance W, casts a shadow scaled W / z about the light's axis; turning the object turns its shadow exactly, because the shadow is the same flat pieces drawn a second time through a planar projection matrix (matrix3d from the light position onto the wall plane), filled in ink at 45-60 %. Penumbra: two copies of the shadow layer, sharp and one with a constant 14 px blur, mixed by defocusMix of (W - z) / z; never an animated blur radius. The wall itself is a mid-tone plane with a plate-light falloff around the light's axis.

directions.name: The fold
directions.idea: Every shot is printed on one sheet, and the film moves on by folding it.

story.line: The problem is printed on the sheet; each fold puts one step behind it; the last fold leaves the result face up.

world.set: One cool sheet fills the frame, seen from a low three-quarter angle as if it lay on an unseen table. Everything is printed on it at true scale (the product panel, a chart, the words), so a crease can run straight through a word or a row.
world.planes: 2-3: the sheet, the half that folds, and the reverse face it reveals
world.light: A folding half shades with its angle to one fixed key: turned 90 degrees away it sits 0.14 L below the flat sheet, and it lands back one step lighter than it left.
world.light_build: face-shade method on the two faces of the folding half (one ink overlay each, opacity from n.l); the flat sheet carries no overlay.
world.texture: clean, with a 1.5 px crease hairline in the ink colour at 20 %

palettes.notes: the sheet is the ground, tinted toward the accent hue; ink is printed matter; the accent marks the one printed thing that changed
a mid stone sheet on a darker table step; the reverse face is one step darker than the front
a neutral paper with one material (a fine paper texture used everywhere)

type_options.notes: printed, calm; line 84 and display 128 only
tight tracking on display, a printed look

camera.animator: The sheet folds, creases and unfolds; the camera only leans in and drifts.
camera.in_shot: A slow dolly toward the next crease line (creep 3-6 % per second) with a 1-2 degree lean.
camera.between: Inside an act there are no cuts: the sheet folds along a crease and its back is the next shot. Act changes are velocity cuts on the fastest frame of a fold.

cuts.grammar: Folds are the seams (morph and mask); hard cuts only on the music's two biggest accents.
cuts.on_sound: A fold lands flat on a soft accent; the fold itself is silent until it lands.

type.scale_contrast: Lines at 84 against the printed product at full frame; one giant word (900) printed across a crease so the fold cuts it in half.
type.behaviour: Words are printed on the sheet and fold with it, but never while being read: a fold starts after the reading hold.

signature.name: The crease fold
signature.shot: A 1.5 px crease draws diagonally across a full-frame product panel in 10 f. The far half lifts toward the camera about the crease, 0 to 180 degrees in 26 f on stdInOut, shading with its angle to the key; at 90 degrees it stands nearly edge-on with a 2 px paper edge, and as it lands flat its reverse face shows the next shot, printed and already moving.
signature.build: The static half is a plain layer with its own clip-path polygon (one side of the crease). The moving half is a preserve-3d wrapper rotating about the crease axis (transform-origin on the crease, rotate3d along the crease direction) with no clip-path, mask or overflow on the wrapper, because any of them flattens the 3D. It holds two faces, front and reverse (backface-visibility hidden, the reverse turned 180 degrees), and each face carries its own clip-path polygon for its half. Shading from the face-shade method; a third 2 px edge face shows only between 80 and 100 degrees.

signature_alt.name: The accordion
signature_alt.shot: The sheet pleats into six vertical strips that fold like a fan down to one strip, then fans open as the next shot.
signature_alt.build: Six strips, each a preserve-3d wrapper turning on rotateY about its own edge with alternating sign, staggered 2 f; clip-paths on the faces inside each strip, never on a wrapper.

lockup.shot: The sheet folds in half twice more, each fold faster (18 f, then 12 f), down to a small square that is the mark printed on its last face; the name prints beside it as the square lands flat.
lockup.build: The same fold rig at a smaller size; the supplied logo as SVG printed on the last face; the name in Words on the sheet plane.

idea_sentences: In this film, [the product's own document or record] becomes the sheet that folds one shot into the next.
In this film, [the step the product saves you] becomes a crease: the sheet folds that step away.
In this film, [what the product brings together] becomes two halves of one sheet folding into each other.

music.feel: measured, papery percussion or a light groove with space between hits

skeleton.picture: Frame 0: a close, low view along the sheet; a printed line of the problem slides under the camera.
The first crease: the problem half folds away and the product is printed on its back.
The diagonal crease fold across the full product panel.
Two smaller folds, each a step the product takes; between them the camera leans in on the printed result.
Two last folds down to the square that is the mark; the name prints beside it.

avoid: crumpled or textured craft paper, kraft or warm paper tones
folding while a line is being read
more than one fold moving at a time
origami animals or other literal craft props
a clip-path or overflow on a rotating 3D wrapper (it flattens the fold)

hook.picture: Frame 0: the version number printed full-bleed on the sheet, its digits cropped by the frame, the camera already sliding along the paper; a crease starts to draw through the last digit.

change.picture: Each change is printed on the next face: the sheet folds over a crease in 14-18 f and the change is already live on the face that lands, one control moving as the fold settles.

copy.what: the change, as a product fact

change.handoff: the next fold starts from the edge of the face that just landed, so the crease carries the motion across

payoff.picture: The crease fold: the whole changed product opens on one full-frame face, the far half lifting about the crease and shading with its angle to the key.

end.picture: The sheet folds down to the mark in two faster folds (18 f, then 12 f); the name and the version print beside it on the last face.

directions.name: Noon relief
directions.idea: The product's screen is cast as a relief in one matte material, and a moving sun decides what the viewer sees.

story.line: A raking light shows every raised thing at once; the light climbs, the shadows give up, and only the one thing the product surfaces keeps its shadow.

world.set: The product's interface cast as a shallow bas-relief in one matte material: every element raised 4-40 px by its importance, seen from a high three-quarter camera. One low key rakes across it, so the screen reads in long shadows before it reads as a screen.
world.planes: 3: the floor plane, the raised elements, and their cast shadows
world.light: One key: elevation 3-72 degrees, azimuth swinging 10-30 degrees per shot; shadow length = height x cot(elevation); faces toward the key +0.08 L, faces away -0.10 L, all one hue.
world.light_build: relief method: blocks as SVG polygons, one shadow path per frame in a group at opacity 0.18; the key's elevation and azimuth are two functions of the frame.
world.texture: the material's own fine grain as one static plate at 2 % (a mid stone or a deep slate), keyed to nothing

palettes.notes: the relief and the floor are one mid stone; shadows are ink at 18 %; the surfaced element's top face carries the accent
a slate relief; lit faces one step lighter; type near-white, debossed into the floor
the whole relief in the accent's own hue at depth; the surfaced element lifts to the light accent step

type_options.sans: a humanist sans at a light weight
type_options.notes: quiet, debossed into the floor 1 px
raised 2 px like the interface, so the key shades it too

camera.animator: The light: the key climbs, swings and settles; the camera is locked high and only creeps.
camera.in_shot: A creep of 2-4 % per second toward the brightest element; the key never stops moving (0.5-2 degrees per second).
camera.between: The key drops to 3 degrees, the relief falls to near dark (a light seam), and the next shot rises with the key; act changes cut on the music.

cuts.grammar: Seams carried by the light: the key sinks and rises across them; hard cuts only on the music's entries.
cuts.on_sound: The noon lift lands on the track's entry; a light seam carries no sound.

type.scale_contrast: A small debossed line (84) on the floor against a relief that fills the frame; the payoff only one step larger (display 128).
type.behaviour: A fragment is debossed into the floor and becomes readable when the key rakes across it; the key holds still for its reading hold.

signature.name: The noon lift
signature.shot: Under a key at 8 degrees every raised element throws a shadow 4-5 times its height across the floor. The key climbs to 72 degrees in 1.2 s on stdInOut: every shadow shrinks under 15 px, while the one element the product surfaces rises from 40 to 260 px over the same 1.2 s, so its shadow alone stays long (about 85 px) and it ends the tallest, sharpest thing in the frame.
signature.build: Relief method: up to 300 blocks as SVG polygons painted back to front, one shadow path per frame (each block's footprint hull moved h x cot(e) along the key azimuth) in a group at opacity 0.18; e(f) and the surfaced block's h(f) on the same stdInOut curve; face fills from face-shade with the key vector; no CSS 3D and no filters on the blocks.

signature_alt.name: The rising relief
signature_alt.shot: The relief starts flat, no heights and no shadows, under a key at 15 degrees; every element rises to its height in order of importance with a 3 f stagger, growing its shadow as it rises, the surfaced element last and tallest.
signature_alt.build: The same relief method; each block's h(f) on settleOut from its rank; shadows follow h.

lockup.shot: The mark is cast in the same relief, 60 px high, at the centre of a cleared floor; the key settles at 35 degrees and the name lies on the floor beside it, debossed 1 px.
lockup.build: The supplied logo's outline as a footprint in the relief method; the name in Words with a 1 px inset shadow on the floor plane.

idea_sentences: In this film, [the one thing the product surfaces among many] becomes the only shadow left at noon.
In this film, [the product's interface] becomes a relief that the light reads in order of importance.
In this film, [what the product makes visible] becomes the moment a low sun reaches it.

music.feel: slow and spacious; a low pulse or held bass that opens when the light climbs

skeleton.picture: Frame 0: a relief in near darkness, the key at 3 degrees, one ridge catching light and sliding.
The key lifts to 20 degrees: the interface reads tallest first.
The key swings in azimuth; each element in turn throws the longest shadow.
The noon lift: every shadow gives up except the surfaced element's.
The floor clears; the mark stands in relief, the name debossed beside it.

avoid: warm sunlight, tungsten or a sunset hue
visible beams, rays or haze
shadows in a second hue or that darken twice where they overlap
glossy or metallic materials
a key light that jumps instead of travelling

hook.picture: Frame 0: the version number cast in the matte slab under a key at 8 degrees, each digit throwing a shadow four times its height; the key starts to climb.

change.picture: Each change is one raised element of the product relief: it rises out of the floor (40 to 120 px in 20 f), its shadow growing with it while the key holds low and rakes its edge.

copy.what: the change, as a product fact

change.handoff: the camera trucks along the floor to the next raised element while the last one sinks back as it passes

payoff.picture: The noon lift: the key climbs to 72 degrees in 1.2 s, every shadow shrinks, and the whole updated screen stands as one relief with the newest element keeping the only long shadow.

end.picture: The mark cast in the same relief on a cleared floor, the key settling at 35 degrees; the name and the version lie debossed beside it.

directions.name: Macro bench
directions.idea: The product made physical and seen through a macro lens: materials and focus, not cuts, move the story.

story.line: Open on a surface too close to name; each rack pulls back one step until the detail is understood as part of the product.

world.set: The product's parts as physical materials at macro scale: a control in matte silicone, an anodised edge with brushed micro-streaks, a printed card whose ink shows its dot structure. Three to five depth planes, each a baked texture plate (never a flat vector), one sharp at a time.
world.planes: 3-5 depth planes of textured material, one sharp at a time
world.light: One soft key from the upper left at 30 degrees: the brushed edge carries a narrow sheen band that slides along the grain as the camera slides; matte parts only shade; printed dots read as tone until sharp.
world.light_build: Each plane a baked texture still (rendered at 2x once) plus one sheen plate (a narrow dithered one-hue band) clipped to the brushed part and moved by transform at 1.4x the camera slide.
world.texture: the materials themselves: brushed streaks, a dot screen in the print, matte silicone grain; softened copies turn texture into tone

palettes.notes: cool anodised grey and matte silicone; only the sharp plane carries full ink and the accent
white matte materials; the accent arrives late, on the plane the story ends on
dark anodised slate; the sheen band is the lightest thing in frame

type_options.notes: crisp counters that survive macro crops

type_options.sans: a technical sans with a mono partner for numbers
type_options.notes: tabular figures; mono only for product strings

camera.animator: Focus: a rack between planes carries attention and hides changes.
camera.in_shot: A slider move at macro scale, 0.5-1.5 px/f, with parallax between the planes and the sheen sliding along the grain.
camera.between: Defocus seams: the outgoing shot throws out of focus, the cut lands inside the softness and the new plane snaps sharp; a defocus pulse hides a jump in scale.

cuts.grammar: Carried by focus: defocus cuts and rack hand-offs, never a crossfade.
cuts.on_sound: The snap to sharp sits on a soft accent; the throw out of focus has no sound.

type.scale_contrast: Type at macro scale (hero 240, cropped by the frame, printed with its dot screen) against tiny product details, then one line at reading size in the sharp plane.
type.behaviour: Type sits on its own depth plane and is read only when sharp; it racks into focus instead of rising.

signature.name: The focus relay
signature.shot: A brushed edge 3 px wide on the product fills the left third at 40x, sharp, its streaks catching the sheen; behind it the product is soft tone. The focus racks through three planes in 30 f (the edge, a middle row of printed dots, the far panel), and on frame 15, where the middle plane is softest, its content changes, so the far plane snaps sharp already in its next state.
signature.build: RackFocus with levels from lib/defocus (two pre-softened copies of each textured plate at most, weighted by defocusMix), the hero slot outside the softened stack; planes as sibling layers moved by parallax(); the swap on rackState's softest frame; the sheen plate rides with the edge layer.

signature_alt.name: The defocus pulse jump
signature_alt.shot: The whole frame softens for 7 f and resolves at x1.24 onto a detail of the same object.
signature_alt.build: defocusPulse with a scale jump on its softest frame.

lockup.shot: The mark is embossed in the material at macro scale and racks sharp out of soft tone; a pull back of x6 shows it small on the product's corner, the name printed beside it with its dot screen.
lockup.build: The supplied logo as an embossed texture plate (baked once) in the RackFocus stack; the pull back on lmix; the name in Words.

idea_sentences: In this film, [the detail the product gets right] becomes the one plane in focus.
In this film, [what the product is made of] becomes a material seen closer than anyone looks.
In this film, [the small part that does the big job] becomes a macro shot where it fills the frame.

music.feel: intimate and close; a soft electronic pulse with detail in the high end

skeleton.picture: Frame 0: a macro of brushed streaks with the sheen already sliding; nothing nameable yet.
The focus relay through three planes; the content changes in the softest frame.
A slow slide across the printed dots: the product's result, sharp.
A pull back with the planes sliding apart, all sharp for the first time.
The embossed mark racks sharp; the pull back shows it on the product.

avoid: animated CSS blur radius on large layers
flat vectors pre-softened to fake a lens: soften textured plates
lens dust or out-of-focus highlight circles
reading text while it is soft
chrome or mirror finishes

hook.picture: Frame 0: the version numerals embossed in the product material at 40x, a focus plane crossing them while a 3 px brushed edge catches the sheen.

change.picture: Each change is one physical detail of the product at macro scale: focus racks onto it in 18 f and the change works in that detail (a switch throws, a surface lights) while the rest stays soft tone.

copy.what: the change, as a product fact

change.handoff: focus moves to the next detail over 12 f before the camera follows, so the rack leads every handover

payoff.picture: The focus relay: three planes rack in 30 f, the edge, the change, the product, and the last plane holds the whole updated product sharp.

end.picture: The mark embossed at macro scale racks sharp out of soft tone; a pull back of x6 shows it on the product corner with the name and the version printed below.

directions.name: One surface
directions.idea: Every state of the product lives on one huge surface; the film is a single camera journey across it.

story.line: One continuous trip across the product's map, each region a stop, until the camera leaves the ground and the whole map is the answer.

world.set: One very large flat canvas, 5-12 frames wide, holds every shot as a region (the problem, each proof, the payoff), laid out like a plan and joined by the product's own connectors.
world.planes: 2: the canvas and a slower ground plane under it (parallax on log scale)
world.light: One low key from the upper left rakes across the canvas: every region on it throws a short shadow away from the key, and the canvas carries a very subtle falloff from the key side (0.05 L across the frame) that stays put while the camera travels; at the reveal the whole surface lifts one exposure step. No pool follows the camera.
world.light_build: relief method for the regions' shadows from the one key; plate-light method for the static key falloff under the canvas; the reveal an exposure lift of 0.10 over 0.9 s.
world.texture: clean

palettes.notes: regions as raised surfaces with the paper shadow; connectors in ink; the accent marks the route travelled
a mid slate canvas; regions one step lighter; connectors near-white
a dark stage; raised regions one step lighter with a top hairline

type_options.notes: three sizes printed on the canvas; scale comes from the camera
a plan-like, drawn feel

camera.animator: The camera: whips, pull-backs and reframes between regions; the regions themselves barely move.
camera.in_shot: Near-holds drift 30 px/s; chained reframes with a 5 % scale pulse.
camera.between: No cuts: a whip with a copy swap on its peak, a zoom-out hop, a pull back that reverses into a push.

cuts.grammar: One take: carried velocity everywhere; at most one hard cut, on the music's biggest accent.
cuts.on_sound: Whip peaks and arrivals sit on the music's accents; travel itself carries no sound.

type.scale_contrast: Type is printed on the canvas at three sizes, and the camera's scale does the rest: a hero word seen from far reads as a line, a line seen close fills the frame.
type.behaviour: Copy belongs to its region and is read only when the camera has settled there; a swap happens on a whip's peak.

signature.name: The whole-map reveal
signature.shot: After the proof, the camera pulls back in one log-scale move, x30 over 3 s on strongInOut: every shot the viewer has seen is still there, running, as one region of a single plan joined by the product's connectors, and the pull settles over its last 20 f on the whole surface, which reads as the product's own shape.
signature.build: One large flat layer drawn at the size of its biggest view, regions as children with their own state functions, one camera transform through camera(shot); regions below 0.25 scale swap to a static still; reversal() for the pull that turns into the last push.

signature_alt.name: The corner bank
signature_alt.shot: The camera rides behind a connector's lead point across the surface; at a rounded corner it banks 6 degrees into the turn and swings round with the line, and as it straightens the connector opens onto the next region.
signature_alt.build: An SVG path on the canvas (stroke-dashoffset with pathLength 1) and a head point from a table sampled once at build time; the camera targets the head with a lag (carry with decay); the roll eased on stdInOut.

lockup.shot: The pull reverses into a last push onto one more region of the surface, the one that holds the mark printed at region size; the camera settles and creeps.
lockup.build: The supplied logo as an SVG region on the canvas; reversal() into the push; the name in Words printed beside it on the canvas.

idea_sentences: In this film, [the product's own map, board or plan] becomes the one surface every shot lives on.
In this film, [how the product connects its parts] becomes the route the camera travels.
In this film, [everything the product holds] becomes a surface the camera can show whole only at the end.

music.feel: a steady groove that keeps moving; the bass carries the travel

skeleton.picture: Frame 0: close on one region, already moving; the camera drifts.
A whip along a connector to the second region; the copy swaps on the whip's peak.
A reframe chain lands the first proof region at reading size.
A zoom-out hop to the next region; its result already running.
The whole-map reveal.
The pull reverses into a push onto the region that holds the mark.

avoid: a canvas of empty filler regions or placeholder blocks
cuts that break the single take
whips past about 80 px/f on readable content
globe or world-map clichés
reading text while the camera travels

hook.picture: Frame 0: the camera already gliding over the surface across a region printed with the version number at region size.

change.picture: Each change is one region of the surface: the camera glides to it on one strongInOut move of 1.2-1.6 s and the region runs its product state as it arrives.

copy.what: the change, as a product fact

change.handoff: the glide never stops between regions; the next region enters the frame edge while the current one still runs

payoff.picture: The whole-map reveal: a log-scale pull back of x12 over 2 s shows every change as one region of a single plan, all of them running.

end.picture: A last push onto the region that holds the mark at region size; the name and the version set in that region; the camera settles and creeps.

directions.name: Depth dive
directions.idea: The film flies forward through stacked planes of the product; every plane passed is a step left behind.

story.line: The flight starts already moving and only gets faster between reads, until it brakes dead on the one screen that matters.

world.set: A field that reads as thirty to forty planes, each a real state of the product (a screen with its type, a card with its data, a statement, a mark), floating at different depths in one clean void, facing the camera. Near ones swell and slide off the edges; far ones barely drift. A far plane is smaller and softer but keeps its own colours and content, never dimmed into a blank shape; no plane is a blank card, and nothing else floats in the void.
world.planes: 12 live plane slots, recycled so the field reads as 30-40 planes
world.light: The arrival plane lands square to the lens at full contrast; the planes behind it soften one focus step. The void stays clean: no pool of light, no haze, no lit patch behind the line.
world.light_build: exposure-plate method on the arrival plane (its own plate lifts 0.10 over 0.6 s); each plane's focus level set once at build time (no depth dimming toward the ground).
world.texture: clean

palettes.notes: a dark void; planes are raised steps with top hairlines; the accent is the arrival plane
a void in the accent's own hue at depth; far planes soften in it, keeping their content, the arrival plane is near-white
a white void; depth reads by size and a soft shadow per plane

type_options.notes: giant type planes as texture, lines at 84 on the arrival plane
fast and plain

camera.animator: The camera: a forward flight that never stops; speed is the expression, slow in the reads, fast between them.
camera.in_shot: A forward drift in log depth at reading speed (the next plane approaching at 3 px/f or less on its text).
camera.between: Fly-through: a plane passes the lens and the next one is the new frame (zoom-through seams); the flight speed is carried across every cut.

cuts.grammar: Carried velocity: zoom-throughs and velocity cuts; never a cut from rest.
cuts.on_sound: A whoosh peaks on the plane passing the lens; the arrival lands on a hit.

type.scale_contrast: Planes of giant type (900) pass the lens as texture; the read line sits on the plane the flight slows for.
type.behaviour: The flight slows to a near hold for each fragment, then accelerates away (a launch exit into the next pass).

signature.name: The field flythrough
signature.shot: The camera accelerates through the field in 2 s, passing about thirty planes, each a real state of the product. Near planes swell past the frame edges on both sides while far ones barely move, and the flight brakes over its last 18 f as one plane arrives square to the lens at 100 % of the frame: the hero screen, already alive.
signature.build: CSS 3D: one preserve-3d stage, 12 plane slots as flat layers at translateZ (perspective 1200-1800 px); the camera is the stage's translateZ on one exponential approach in log depth; when a slot passes behind the lens it jumps to the far end with the next state, so 12 elements read as 30-40; planes beyond six frames are static stills.

signature_alt.name: The brake and peek
signature_alt.shot: The flight brakes 40 px short of a plane; the plane tips up 12 degrees like a lifted page, showing the next one under it, and the flight carries on through the gap in 14 f.
signature_alt.build: One plane's rotateX on spr while the stage's translateZ carries its speed through the gap (carry).

lockup.shot: The last plane is the mark; the flight stops dead on it on the final hit with no settle, and the name sits on the same plane; one quiet creep of 1 % per second until the end.
lockup.build: The supplied logo as SVG on the last plane slot; the stop is the approach curve hitting its target on the hit frame; the name in Words; creep for the end hold.

directions.name: Rollout
directions.idea: The frame is a wall of three hundred double-sided tiles, and every change the product makes rolls across them.

story.line: One tile turns, then a wave carries the change to all of them; four waves, four changes, the last one claiming the whole wall in the accent.

world.set: About 300 square tiles (20 x 15 at 1080p, 2 px ink gaps) are the whole frame, the wall turned 8 degrees to the camera so a turning tile shows depth. Each tile has a front and a back; together the fronts show one picture (the product now) and the backs the next. The held shape (the device) is drawn across them.
world.planes: 3: the tile wall, the turning tiles lifted off it, and the held shape
world.light: Tiles shade by their angle to one key: a tile at 90 degrees is 0.18 L darker, and lands one step brighter, so every wave reads as a band of shade crossing the wall.
world.light_build: face-shade method on each tile's two faces: one ink overlay per face, opacity from n.l.
world.texture: clean; tile gaps on whole pixels

palettes.notes: paper and ink pictures alternate wave by wave; the fourth wave turns up the accent backs
a mid slate wall; the accent flood is the only full-chroma field in the film
a deep-hue wall; pictures in near-white; the flood lifts to the light accent step

type_options.sans: a grotesk at a heavy weight
type_options.notes: hero words built across tiles, one per wave
plain and loud

camera.animator: The tiles: waves of turns carry every change; the camera is locked and only creeps.
camera.in_shot: A creep of 3-6 % per second toward the held shape while the wall stands still.
camera.between: A wave of turns is the seam: the next shot is on the tiles' backs; act changes cut on downbeats.

cuts.grammar: Cuts on sound: every wave starts on a downbeat; the waves themselves carry the change.
cuts.on_sound: A soft click per diagonal, never per tile; the flood on the drop.

type.scale_contrast: One hero word (240) built across the tiles per wave against the small held shape; the payoff in giant (900), cropped by the frame.
type.behaviour: Words turn with the tiles but never mid-read: a wave waits for the reading hold to end.

signature.name: The flood roll
signature.shot: On the downbeat at the turn the tile under the held shape's centre turns first; a diagonal wave spreads from it, each tile turning 180 degrees about its vertical axis in 8 f with a 1 f stagger per diagonal step, so the whole wall has turned in 42 f. Tiles shade as they pass 90 degrees and land one step brighter, and their backs are the accent: the wall becomes one accent field from the shape outward.
signature.build: tile-field method: 300 divs in one preserve-3d wall (perspective 2000 px), each with two faces (backface-visibility hidden), each face showing its slice of the full picture by background-position (one still per state, rendered once); delay = (|col - c0| + |row - r0|) x 1 f; shading from face-shade; 600 faces in all.

signature_alt.name: The column roll
signature_alt.shot: Columns of tiles turn top to bottom about their horizontal axis, left to right across the wall, each column 6 f behind the one before.
signature_alt.build: The same tile field with rotateX; delay = col x 6 f + row x 0.5 f.

lockup.shot: A last roll turns every tile to the plain ground except those under the mark's silhouette, which stay in ink: the mark built of tiles; then its tiles close their gaps from 2 px to 0 over 12 f.
lockup.build: The same tile field; a mask of the supplied logo decides which tiles keep the ink face; gaps from tile size; the name in Words beside it.

directions.name: Cut and paste
directions.idea: An unseen hand assembles the film from cut-out pieces of the product at 16 frames a second while the camera glides at 60.

story.line: Scraps pile up as the problem; the hand builds them into the product; the last pieces are the name.

world.set: An overhead table of one cool ground. Flat cut-out pieces of the product (panels, words, numbers, the mark's parts) with crisp edges and a one-step shadow are placed, swapped and stacked in 2-4 piece layers.
world.planes: 3-4: the table, the piece layers, and the smooth camera over them
world.light: When the collage completes, the table lifts one step lighter for 0.5 s; one exposure event per act.
world.light_build: exposure-plate method (a lift of 0.12 over 0.5 s) on the table layer only, outside the stepped cadence.
world.texture: clean edges; a global grain at 1.5 % keyed to the output frame, so the stepped cadence reads as made

palettes.notes: pieces in ink, mid grey and paper; one accent piece per shot
a neutral paper with a fine grain
a mid stone table; pieces in paper-white and ink, so every piece reads against the ground

type_options.sans: a grotesk in two widths of one family
type_options.notes: words cut as pieces at different sizes
clean cut edges

camera.animator: The pieces: births, swaps and stacks on a 16 fps cadence; the camera glides smoothly at 60 above them, two cadences at once.
camera.in_shot: A slow overhead push or truck at 60 fps.
camera.between: Stepped seams: the table is cleared or covered piece by piece; a hard cut on a beat at most once per act.

cuts.grammar: Stepped: the collage builds and clears on its own cadence; act changes cut on sound.
cuts.on_sound: Pieces land on 16th notes; one sound per landing class, never one per piece.

type.scale_contrast: Words are cut-out pieces at different sizes in one family (line to hero); a word may arrive as three pieces in three frames.
type.behaviour: A fragment is placed whole on the beat and then holds perfectly still (only the camera moves) through its read.

signature.name: The stop-motion build
signature.shot: Over 2 s, on a 16 fps cadence, cut-out pieces of the product land one by one at irregular 2-6 frame gaps, each at 100 % size and opacity on its first frame, stacking into the full product screen, while the camera pushes in smoothly at 60 fps, x1.15 over the whole build.
signature.build: The collage layer reads its frame through stepFrame(f, {animFps: 16}) so it holds each pose for its 16 fps step; the camera layer reads the plain frame; the landing schedule from irregular() (seeded); pieces as flat divs with the paper shadow; the range declared as stepped.

signature_alt.name: The clear-down
signature_alt.shot: The finished collage is taken apart in reverse on the same 16 fps cadence, leaving the one piece the story is about alone on the table.
signature_alt.build: The build schedule run backwards with the one piece excluded; stepFrame on the collage layer.

lockup.shot: The name arrives as cut-out letters placed one per 16 fps step at irregular gaps, the mark's parts last; the camera keeps gliding over the still letters.
lockup.build: Each letter of the name as a piece (Words supplies the metrics); the same stepFrame cadence and irregular() schedule; the supplied logo split into its parts as pieces.

directions.name: Wells
directions.idea: The product's modules are wells sunk into one slab; the one that matters rises out of it toward the lens.

story.line: A board of live modules; one rises and fills the frame, and inside it is the next board, one level deeper.

world.set: A thick slab of one mid-tone material fills the frame, seen from 30 degrees above; a 3 x 4 grid of square wells 40-80 px deep is cut into it, each holding a live part of the product on its floor. A raking key at 20-30 degrees fills each well with a crisp shadow from its upper wall.
world.planes: 3: the slab top, the well floors with their content, and the risen cell
world.light: One key at 20-30 degrees: each well's upper wall throws a shadow across its floor (depth x cot(elevation)); a rising floor leaves its shadow and gains its own on the slab.
world.light_build: relief method: well walls and floors as SVG polygons; each inner shadow a polygon from the wall height; one shadow group at opacity 0.2.
world.texture: the slab material as one static grain plate at 2 %

palettes.notes: a mid stone slab; well floors one step lighter; the risen cell carries the accent edge
a slate slab; content in near-white on the floors
a pale slab; shadows in ink at 16 %

type_options.sans: a technical sans with a mono partner

camera.animator: The slab: floors rise and sink on the beat; the camera is locked except for one log-scale push at each rise.
camera.in_shot: Content creeps inside its well at 2-4 % per second; the key drifts 1 degree per second.
camera.between: A rise fills the frame and the next board is inside it; other changes step on sound.

cuts.grammar: Stepped and on sound: layout changes on music accents; one carried rise per act.
cuts.on_sound: Steps on 8th notes; the rise on a downbeat with a low thud as it locks.

type.scale_contrast: Giant numerals (900) on one well floor against caption labels (46) on the slab: about x20.
type.behaviour: Type sits on well floors in whole modules; nothing slides between wells while being read.

signature.name: The rise
signature.shot: One well's floor rises 80 px in 24 f on settleOut until its content stands proud of the slab, while the other eleven floors sink 30 px and their shadows deepen; the camera pushes in on a log curve, x3.2 over the same 24 f, so the risen cell fills the frame and its content is the next board, already sunk into wells.
signature.build: Relief method in SVG: each well is four inner wall polygons and a floor; a well of depth d throws an inner shadow d x cot(e) long; the rising floor is d going negative (a raised block with its own cast shadow); the board grid steps with HardStep, cell content reflows with MorphChain and the inner board opens through Window; the camera framing from morphBox.

signature_alt.name: The sink
signature_alt.shot: Every floor but one sinks 60 px in a 2 f stagger from the chosen well outward, so the one left at the slab surface reads as lifted without moving.
signature_alt.build: The same relief rig; floor depth per well from its distance to the chosen one.

lockup.shot: The last rise lifts a cell whose floor carries the mark cut into it as a shallow relief; the key swings 15 degrees and the mark's edges catch it; the name on the slab beside the cell.
lockup.build: The supplied logo's outline as a recessed footprint in the relief method; the name in Words.

directions.name: Monument type
directions.idea: The product's name, set so large it becomes the set; the camera travels its letterforms.

story.line: Start inside a stroke where nothing reads; travel the letters, look inside one; pull back until the word is the name.

world.set: The product's name at giant scale (900 px and up, cropped by the frame) is the architecture: the camera moves along its strokes, counters and edges, and product details live inside the counters and on the letter faces.
world.planes: 2-3: the giant word, a second word layer at a slower rate, and the product inside the counters
world.light: The product inside a counter is the light source: its light falls on the counter's inner rim as a one-hue plate 0.10 L brighter, and the counter the camera pushes into is the brightest field in the film.
world.light_build: One rim plate per lit counter (a dithered plate clipped to the counter outline, opacity following how lit the product is).
world.texture: clean

directions.name: Census
directions.idea: Hundreds of the product's own units fill the frame; the film is what the product does to all of them at once.

story.line: One unit's pain, then the camera rises to show four hundred like it; the product sorts them all in one pass.

world.set: A field of hundreds of the product's units (rows, tickets, files, alerts, each a small real object with its state) lies on a floor plane. Seen from overhead it reads flat; as the camera cranes down it recedes to a horizon. The field sorts, groups, filters and ranks in waves.
world.planes: 2-3: the floor field, the lifted unit, and the line band the field clears
world.light: A soft pool rides with the wave front: sorted units lie in the light, unsorted ones in the falloff 0.10 L darker, so the front reads as light arriving.
world.light_build: plate-light method: one long pool plate translated with the front's position.
world.texture: clean

lockup.build: The same list sinking (translateY and opacity) on a stagger by distance from the hero slot; the supplied logo as SVG in the hero slot; the name in Words.

directions.name: Turntable
directions.idea: The product is one solid object with real weight; it turns under a fixed light, and its back holds what comes next.

story.line: The finished object first, heavy and still; then it turns, face by face, to show how it got there.

world.set: The product as a solid block (its screen or the mark, with a real depth of 15-25 % of its width) standing on an endless matte floor under one fixed key; it casts a shadow that swings and stretches as it turns.
world.planes: 3: the floor, the solid, and its cast shadow
world.light: One fixed key at 35 degrees elevation: every face shades by its angle to the key, so a turn reads as faces passing through the light; the cast shadow is the footprint offset by height x cot(elevation).
world.light_build: face-shade method on the six faces of the box; the shadow one SVG polygon under it at opacity 0.2.
world.texture: clean, with a 1 px key-side edge hairline

palettes.notes: a mid stone floor; the block's sides one and two steps darker than its face
a slate floor; the face lit, the sides in shade
a pale floor; shadow in ink at 18 %

type_options.notes: printed on the face, never sheared past 7 degrees
a quieter object

camera.animator: The object turns with weight; the camera orbits slowly the other way.
camera.in_shot: An orbit of 6-12 degrees per shot with a slow push.
camera.between: A half-turn brings the back to the camera; a press tilt hides a state change.

cuts.grammar: Carried: turns and press tilts; no hard cuts inside the object's story.
cuts.on_sound: A soft rumble under the turn; the landing carries one low knock.

type.scale_contrast: Type on the block's face at display size against one line on the floor beside it.
type.behaviour: Text is printed on a face only while it faces the camera; a turn starts after the reading hold.

signature.name: The weighted half-turn
signature.shot: The block turns 180 degrees in 40 f with inertia: fast for the first 12 f, a long settle, a 2-degree overshoot back on landing. Its four side faces sweep through the key and shade by angle, its shadow swings and stretches with the footprint, and the face that ends square to the lens is its real back, which carries the next state.
signature.build: A preserve-3d box of six real faces (front, back and four sides at true depth; backface-visibility hidden), rotateY from inertia() with the landing overshoot from spr over the last 10 f; one face-shade overlay per face from the key vector; the cast shadow one SVG polygon (the rotated footprint moved h x cot(e)) at opacity 0.2 under the box; no thin-layer edge stack, no moving highlight.

signature_alt.name: The press tilt swap
signature_alt.shot: A press tips the block 8 degrees toward the point pressed; the content changes on the tilt's peak frame.
signature_alt.build: pressAt() driving a rotate3d toward the press point; the face-shade overlays follow the tilt.

lockup.shot: The block turns a last quarter and shrinks on the floor into the mark as a solid, its shadow settling under it; the name prints on the floor beside it.
lockup.build: The same box rig with the supplied logo on its face, scaled on settleOut; the name in Words on the floor plane.

idea_sentences: In this film, [the product as one solid thing] becomes an object with weight you could pick up.
In this film, [what is behind the product's simple face] becomes the back of a solid block.
In this film, [the product's two sides] become the front and back of one object.

music.feel: rounded and weighty, a clean bass with soft percussion

skeleton.picture: Frame 0: the finished object close, the camera already orbiting past its edge.
The weighted half-turn: its back is the problem it solves.
Two quick quarter-turns, small echoes of the half-turn, each landing a result.
The block rests face-on while the camera orbits 10 degrees round it.
A last quarter turn into the mark as a solid on the floor.

avoid: chrome, metallic or reflective materials
a moving specular band or gloss
a phone or laptop floating in a void
edge stacks of thin layers faking a thickness
spinning the object for show: every turn changes a state

hook.picture: Frame 0: the product block mid-turn under a fixed key; its face carries the version number as it turns square to the lens.

change.picture: Each change is on the next face: the block turns 90 degrees in 30 f with weight and the face that lands shows the change running.

copy.what: the change, as a product fact

change.handoff: every turn starts on the last one settling, so the block never rests between changes

payoff.picture: The weighted half-turn: 180 degrees in 40 f with a 2-degree overshoot back, the far face the whole updated product.

end.picture: The block turns a last quarter and shrinks into the mark as a solid; the name and the version print on the floor beside it.

directions.name: Exploded view
directions.idea: The product comes apart into its layers so the viewer sees how it works, then snaps back whole.

story.line: The interface in use; it comes apart to show the one layer doing the work; it snaps back and the result is simply there.

world.set: A three-quarter view from above of the product's interface on a cool floor. On its key beats the interface separates along depth into 3-7 layers (data, structure, chrome, the one smart layer) with hairline guides between them.
world.planes: 3-7 interface layers along depth, plus the floor
world.light: The smart layer is the light: it lifts to full contrast in the accent and its light falls on the underside of the layer above as a one-hue plate (C 0.10 or less), stopping hard at that layer's edge.
world.light_build: One dithered plate clipped to the layer above (it moves with that layer), opacity tied to the smart layer's lift.
world.texture: clean, with 1.5 px leader lines

palettes.notes: opaque layers with the paper shadow; the smart layer in the accent
raised layers with top hairlines on a dark floor
a mid slate floor; layers one and two steps lighter

type_options.sans: a technical sans with a mono partner
type_options.notes: labels are product strings at caption size
plain statements on the floor plane

camera.animator: The layers separate, slide and rejoin; the camera holds its three-quarter view with one crane at the explode.
camera.in_shot: A slow push of 2-4 % per second; one crane of 10-25 degrees per explode.
camera.between: The stack rejoins flat and turns front-on: the flat UI is the next shot (a shape match).

cuts.grammar: Carried: shape matches from the 3D stack to the flat UI; chapter changes cut on sound.
cuts.on_sound: Each layer's lift is silent; the rejoin lands on one click.

type.scale_contrast: A caption label (46) on a leader line to one layer, and the line role for statements.
type.behaviour: Only one layer is ever labelled, and only after the stack stops; labels are product strings, never filler.

signature.name: The layer explode
signature.shot: The live interface turns to a three-quarter view and its layers lift apart along depth one after another, 60 px apart with a 4 f stagger. The camera cranes 18 degrees between them to the one layer that does the smart part, it lifts in the accent, then the stack snaps back together in 14 f and turns flat to the camera, landing as the frontal product.
signature.build: CSS 3D: each layer a flat sibling in one preserve-3d stage, translateZ per layer on a front-loaded curve with stagger(); leader lines as 1.5 px divs; the rejoin on stdInOut; the turn flat on the stage's rotateX.

signature_alt.name: The lift-out
signature_alt.shot: One control lifts out of its row in the flat interface, turns 30 degrees as it rises 120 px toward the lens and becomes a solid hero object, while the interface sinks one step behind it.
signature_alt.build: The control as a preserve-3d box with real depth; rise and turn on spr; the interface behind dims by an opacity step.

lockup.shot: The layers collapse onto one thin plate that is the mark, the smart layer last; the name on the floor beside it.
lockup.build: The same stage with each layer's translateZ going to 0 on a stagger; the supplied logo as SVG on the plate; the name in Words.

idea_sentences: In this film, [the hidden layer that does the work] becomes the one layer that lifts out of the stack.
In this film, [how the product is built] becomes an exploded view of its interface.
In this film, [what the product adds on top] becomes a new layer sliding into the stack.

music.feel: technical and clean, precise percussion over a steady bass

skeleton.picture: Frame 0: the interface front-on, already in use.
The interface tilts to three-quarter; the problem shows on its surface.
The layer explode to the smart layer.
The stack rejoins flat; the product's result front-on, one leader line on the smart part.
The layers collapse to one thin plate that is the mark.

avoid: isometric clip art or icon diagrams
more than seven layers
labels on every layer
translucent layers: layers are opaque, separated by depth
a slow orbit with nothing happening

hook.picture: Frame 0: the live interface already tilting to three-quarters; its top layer carries the version number.

change.picture: Each change is one layer: the stack lifts apart (60 px, 4 f stagger), the camera cranes 12 degrees to the changed layer and it works on its own plate.

copy.what: the change, as a product fact

change.handoff: the stack closes as the crane moves on, so the next layer lifts from a closed stack

payoff.picture: The layer explode: the whole stack lifts apart and the camera cranes between the layers to the newest one.

end.picture: The layers collapse onto one thin plate that is the mark; the name and the version print on the floor beside it.

directions.name: One shape
directions.idea: One shape keeps becoming the next thing: no cuts, only changes of role.

story.line: The product's one control changes role on every beat, each role causing the next, until it opens into the world it was for.

world.set: A clean ground and one shape (the product's own control: a pill, a bar, a field) that morphs from role to role (progress bar, caret, button, window, card, word container, mark); everything else is born from it or returns to it.
world.planes: 2: the ground and the shape, with the scene inside the shape on its own plane
world.light: The shape lifts one step in lightness on each change of role; its window interior opens a step brighter than the ground.
world.light_build: exposure-plate method inside the shape (a lift of 0.10 per role change) and once on the whole frame when the window opens.
world.texture: clean

palettes.notes: the shape in the accent while it acts, relaxing to ink when it rests
a white world; full colour only inside the opened window
a deep-hue world; the shape is near-white and the light accent step marks its action

type_options.notes: matches the shape's radius
words sit inside the container at line size

camera.animator: The shape swells, collapses, stretches and opens; the camera follows it with a lag and scales with it.
camera.in_shot: The shape breathes (a pill breath) and the camera eases after it.
camera.between: Morph seams only: the shape grows into a window whose interior is the next scene, or collapses to a dot that opens the next.

cuts.grammar: One take: a morph chain with zero hard cuts until the lockup.
cuts.on_sound: Each change of role on a beat; the window opening on the drop.

type.scale_contrast: Type lives inside the shape at line size; the payoff word fills the shape at display size.
type.behaviour: The container morphs to each fragment's width; words never cross-fade between containers.

signature.name: The swell into a window
signature.shot: A small pill holding one word swells by half its width over 12 f, the word leaves, and the pill keeps growing in both axes for 20 f while its corners square to the frame's aspect, so its interior opens as a window onto the next scene, already running; the window's edge leaves the frame on its fastest frame, 100 % wide.
signature.build: Morph over one morphBox (x, y, w, h and radius on one transform) through the role chain; the window is a clip-path inset on the interior sibling layer with corners from the box radius; the breath on swell, the exit at peak speed.

signature_alt.name: The dot relay
signature_alt.shot: The whole scene collapses into one point that travels and opens into the next object.
signature_alt.build: morphBox down to a dot, carry on its travel, Iris out of it.

lockup.shot: The shape collapses from the window into the mark's silhouette in one 18 f move; the name slides out of it.
lockup.build: morphBox into the logo's bounding box, the supplied logo SVG fading in over the last 4 f inside it; the name in Words.

idea_sentences: In this film, [the product's one control: a button, a bar, a field] becomes the shape that becomes everything else.
In this film, [the product's flow from start to done] becomes one shape changing role.
In this film, [what the product turns one thing into] becomes a morph with no cut.

music.feel: fluid and rolling, a smooth bass line with soft percussion; a hole before the last shape

skeleton.picture: Frame 0: the shape as a progress bar, already moving.
The shape becomes a caret, then a field, then a button: one role per beat.
The swell into a window.
Inside the window the shape is the product's control, acting.
The shape collapses into the mark.

avoid: a bare dot as the shape: use the product's own control
cross-fading two copies of the shape
squash and stretch on the container
a second shape competing for the eye
hard cuts before the lockup

hook.picture: Frame 0: a pill holding the version number swells by half its width.

change.picture: Each change is one role of the shape: the pill becomes a button that is pressed, a row that lists the new item, a toggle that flips, one move of 18-24 f each.

copy.what: the change, as a product fact

change.handoff: the last role of one change is the first role of the next, with no cut between them

payoff.picture: The swell into a window: the shape grows past the frame aspect and its interior opens onto the whole updated product.

end.picture: The window collapses into the mark silhouette in 18 f; the name and the version slide out of it.

directions.name: The wall
directions.idea: Sixteen screens of the product in sixteen real moments play on one beat, then slide together into one picture.

story.line: Everyone, everywhere, on one beat; then every panel turns toward the same moment and the wall becomes one frame.

world.set: A wall of 12-24 live panels (4 x 4 at 1080p, 6 x 4 for longer films) with 10 px ink gutters fills the frame; each panel shows the product in a different real moment (a person, a time of day, a device size), all cut to the same beats.
world.planes: 3: the panel wall, each panel's content with its own slow camera, and the gutter grid above both
world.light: Each panel is lit by its own content: when its state changes it lifts 0.06 L for 10 f, so a wave of changes reads as light moving across the wall.
world.light_build: exposure-plate method per panel (a one-step lighter plate inside each clip, opacity per panel).
world.texture: clean; gutters on whole pixels

palettes.notes: dark gutters; each panel keeps the product's own colours inside the house accent
mid slate gutters; the accent marks the panels that just changed, then relaxes
paper gutters; panels framed by a 1 px ink hairline

type_options.notes: one line at a time over the gutters, never inside a panel
friendlier, for people in the panels

camera.animator: The panels: sixteen own cameras on one beat; the wall itself only breathes until the converge.
camera.in_shot: Each panel drifts or creeps in its own direction at 6-30 px/s; the wall breathes 1-2 % in scale.
camera.between: Every panel cuts on the same downbeat; a wave of state changes crosses the wall; the converge closes it into one frame.

cuts.grammar: Cuts on sound: all panels cut together on downbeats; inside a panel, carried moves.
cuts.on_sound: One cut sound for the whole wall, never per panel; the converge on a rising swell that stops as the gutters close.

type.scale_contrast: One line (84) laid over the gutter grid against sixteen small live pictures; one full-width payoff at display size after the converge.
type.behaviour: A fragment sits on a dimmed band across the wall while the panels keep playing behind it.

signature.name: The converge
signature.shot: On the downbeat every panel's camera starts toward one shared picture; over 48 f each panel pans and zooms on its own curve (2 f stagger from the centre outward) until all sixteen show adjacent pieces of one full-frame shot of the product, the gutters close from 10 px to 0 on the last 8 f, and the wall is one frame.
signature.build: tile-field method: 16 clipped panels (overflow hidden), each holding its own scene and, from the converge on, a copy of the final shot placed at the panel's offset in the full frame; each panel's camera is lc(own framing, final framing, t) with t staggered by distance from the centre; content switches to the final shot on the panel's fastest frame; gutters are 10 px ink strips scaled to 0.

signature_alt.name: The state wave
signature_alt.shot: A diagonal front crosses the wall in 24 f; each panel switches from the old way to the product's way as it passes, and the panel lifts one step and relaxes.
signature_alt.build: The same wall; switch frame per panel = t0 + (col + row) x 3 f; exposure plate per panel.

lockup.shot: The one frame pulls back x3 until it is a single panel again in an empty wall of ground; the mark and name sit in the gutter space below it.
lockup.build: One camera transform on lmix; the supplied logo as SVG and the name in Words on the ground.

idea_sentences: In this film, [everyone who uses the product, everywhere] becomes a wall of panels on one beat.
In this film, [the one moment all of them share] becomes the picture every panel turns toward.
In this film, [how many ways the product is used] becomes sixteen screens closing into one.

music.feel: a strong, even beat every panel can lock to; a swell into the converge

skeleton.picture: Frame 0: four panels already playing, more opening on the beat.
The full wall, cutting on downbeats; one line over the gutters.
Every panel cuts on the same downbeat to the product arriving in it.
The converge into one frame.
The frame pulls back to one panel; the mark below it.

avoid: a plain before/after split
panels on different beats
two reads at once
stock-looking people: each panel is a moment of the product in use
a gutter grid that never changes

hook.picture: Frame 0: a wall of sixteen panels, each a moment of the product, the centre panel carrying the version number.

change.picture: Each change fills a block of four panels: they pan and zoom together until they show adjacent pieces of the one state the change makes, then split back.

copy.what: the change, as a product fact

change.handoff: the next block starts to come together while the last one splits

payoff.picture: The converge: all sixteen panels pan and zoom on their own curves into one picture of the new version.

end.picture: The one frame pulls back x3 to a single panel; the mark, the name and the version sit in the gutter below it.

directions.name: Odometer
directions.idea: One number counts through the whole film, and its digits are the set.

story.line: The number climbs with the problem, the product reverses it, and the reels speed up into the one value the product can stand behind.

world.set: Giant digit reels (each digit a masked drum) fill the frame like machinery; the camera rides along and into the drums, and the product's other objects appear as the units being counted.
world.planes: 3: the reel strips, the drum masks, and the unit layer in front
world.light: The drums are cylinders under a key from above: each digit row darkens with its angle on the drum, 0.15 L darker at the window's top and bottom edges, so the numerals visibly turn over a curve.
world.light_build: One static shade plate per drum window (ink, dark at both edges, clear in the middle) above the moving strip; the strip itself never changes tone.
world.texture: clean

palettes.notes: paper numerals on dark drums; the last digit locks in the accent
ink numerals on paper drums
machined mid-stone drums with ink numerals

type_options.sans: a grotesk with strong tabular figures
type_options.notes: numerals drawn once as strips

type_options.sans: a technical sans with tabular figures
type_options.notes: a precise, instrument feel

camera.animator: The reels: drums spin, step and lock; the camera rides down a spinning drum and across to the next.
camera.in_shot: A vertical drift with the reel's motion.
camera.between: A vertical whip down a reel to the next scene (the drum is the cut); a snap zoom out to the whole number.

cuts.grammar: Cuts on the counter's locks, each lock on a music accent; vertical whips carry between them.
cuts.on_sound: Each drum lock is a tick on the beat; the final lock is the hit.

type.scale_contrast: The number at giant size (900) against the read line (84); the unit at caption size tucked under the last digits.
type.behaviour: The number is picture; the words read only while the reels are locked.

signature.name: The reel ride
signature.shot: The camera dives into the last digit's drum while it spins and travels down the reel with it (the numerals stream past as a stepped strip, one numeral per 5 f), slows with the reel over 40 f and lands, square to the lens, on the locked final digit as the whole number snaps into view on a one-frame zoom out of x4.
signature.build: Roll with countSteps per drum (masked drums, numerals drawn once as a tall strip moved by transform, thinned by thinSteps); the camera one transform; the zoom out is SnapZoom's one-frame scale jump with a short defocus; tabular figures throughout.

signature_alt.name: The count that cuts
signature_alt.shot: The counter runs and the film cuts on it mid-count on a music accent, the next shot counting the same number from a new angle.
signature_alt.build: countSteps on one shared clock across the cut.

lockup.shot: The drums roll on past the number into letter strips and lock on the name one drum at a time, left to right, each lock a tick; the mark locks on the first drum.
lockup.build: Each drum's strip (moved by transform) continues into the name's letters and the logo as one glyph; Roll locks on a stagger of 4 f.

idea_sentences: In this film, [the product's one number] becomes the machinery of the film.
In this film, [what the product counts, saves or removes] becomes a reel that never stops turning.
In this film, [the product's result] becomes the digit the reel lands on.

music.feel: mechanical, ticking hats, a pulse that speeds up into the final lock

skeleton.picture: Frame 0: inside a spinning drum, numerals streaming.
The camera pulls out along the reels; the number climbs with the problem.
The product acts: the reels reverse and run down.
The reel ride to the final value.
The drums roll on into the name and lock letter by letter.

avoid: numbers the product cannot back
proportional figures: tabular only
a counter that ticks with no visible cause
slot-machine or casino imagery
spinning reels during a read

hook.picture: Frame 0: inside the drums of the version number, the last digit spinning past the old value.

change.picture: Each change rides a numeral drum: the strip stops on a value and its window opens onto the change as a product moment, the drum shade still on its edges.

copy.what: the change, as a product fact

change.handoff: the next drum already spins at the frame edge while the window closes

payoff.picture: The reel ride: the camera dives into the last digit drum, rides it down for 40 f and lands on the final digit of the new version.

end.picture: The drums roll on into the name and lock letter by letter beside the version; the mark locks on the first drum.

directions.name: Waveform
directions.idea: The product's real sound becomes a landscape, and the camera rides it as it plays.

story.line: A sound plays into noise; the product answers by clearing the ground under it; the sound and the landscape end on the same note.

world.set: The real recorded clip, analysed once at build time into 48 time slices x 64 frequency bands, stands as a landscape of 48 ridges on a floor plane tilted 60 degrees: across is frequency, depth is time, height is energy. The camera rides along time at playback speed, so the ridge under the lens is the instant being heard.
world.planes: 3: the ridge field, the playhead standing across it, and the floor
world.light: The playhead is a thin standing sheet of light across the field: ridges near it lift 0.12 L, falling off over 6 ridges behind and ahead, with no beam and no haze.
world.light_build: Per frame, each ridge's fill lightness = base + 0.12 / (1 + (d / 2)^2), d its distance in ridges from the playhead; the floor falloff from plate-light.
world.texture: clean; 1.5 px ridge lines

palettes.notes: near-white ridge lines on a dark field; the sound's own peaks lift to the accent
a mid slate landscape; the playhead sheet one step lighter
the landscape in the accent's own hue at depth; words in near-white

type_options.notes: each copy fragment printed flat on the floor by the peak it names
plain, so the landscape stays the picture

camera.animator: The sound: the landscape is the clip and the camera rides it at the clip's own speed.
camera.in_shot: A forward ride at playback speed with a slow 3-6 degree crane; it never stops while sound plays.
camera.between: Cuts between words, at the envelope's quiet points, to the next stretch of landscape from a new angle.

cuts.grammar: Cuts on sound: only in the gaps between words; inside a phrase the ride is continuous.
cuts.on_sound: The clip is the soundtrack's lead; the music is chosen to leave its band open and is never lowered under it.

type.scale_contrast: One copy fragment at a time printed on the floor at display size beside the peak it names, against a landscape that fills the frame.
type.behaviour: A fragment lands on the floor beside the peak it names and stays for its reading hold; copy names what the product does to the sound, nothing more.

signature.name: The clean pass
signature.shot: As the sound starts, a front moves with the playhead: every ridge it passes loses its noise floor (bands under the threshold drop to zero height over 6 f), so behind the front (ridges 40 px apart) the field is flat and quiet except the sound's own peaks, which stand up x1.4 as each one plays, a copy fragment printed flat on the floor beside the peak it names.
signature.build: 48 SVG paths (filled ridges painted back to front, fill = ground so nearer ridges hide farther ones, a 1.5 px line in ink); one transform for the floor plane (rotateX 60, perspective 1600 px); heights from the build-time analysis (a json of 48 x 64 energies, never analysed per frame); the camera a translateZ along time at field depth / clip seconds; the noise drop a closed-form ramp per ridge from its time.

signature_alt.name: The word that rises
signature_alt.shot: One peak keeps rising after it plays, up out of the landscape to 3x the frame height in 30 f, and the camera tilts up with it into the next shot.
signature_alt.build: One ridge path's heights scaled by a closed-form curve after its word ends; the camera's pitch follows it with carry; handoffShot at the top.

lockup.shot: The sound's last peak stands up, settles flat, and the name is printed on the floor where it stood, the mark beside it; the ride slows to a creep.
lockup.build: The name's word timing from the same analysis; Words on the floor plane; the supplied logo as SVG; creep.

idea_sentences: In this film, [the product's own recorded sound] becomes a landscape the camera rides.
In this film, [what the product removes from a recording] becomes the ground going flat under the sound.
In this film, [the moments the product hears] become peaks that stand up as they play.

music.feel: sparse, under the clip; a soft pulse that leaves the clip's band empty

skeleton.picture: Frame 0: riding a rough landscape of noise, the playhead already moving.
The sound starts: peaks rise out of the noise as it plays.
The clean pass: the ground goes flat under the sound.
A quiet cut to a new angle; the product's answer as one clean phrase.
The sound's last peak settles into the name on the floor.

avoid: an invented waveform: use the real clip
equaliser bars bouncing to music
a ridgeline poster look: the camera rides, the landscape plays
copy that does not name what the product does to the sound
analysing audio per frame in the render

hook.picture: Frame 0: the camera riding the product sound as a ridged landscape; the version number lies printed on the floor between the ridges.

change.picture: Each change is heard and seen: the playhead front passes and the ridges behind it take the change (cleaner, louder, one band split out) with the product control that did it standing at the front.

copy.what: the change, as a product fact

change.handoff: the playhead never stops; the next change starts wherever it is

payoff.picture: The clean pass: a front moves with the playhead and every ridge behind it loses its noise floor.

end.picture: The last peak settles flat; the name and the version print on the floor where it stood, the mark beside them.

directions.name: Inside the document
directions.idea: The film plays inside the product's own document, and its last full stop opens onto the work the line started.

story.line: The document at true scale; a line is typed; the camera falls into its final full stop, and inside it the product is already working.

world.set: The product's own canvas (an editor, a terminal, a doc, a design file) at true scale, full bleed. The cursor and the caret are the only actors besides the product: edits, selections and insertions move the story.
world.planes: 2: the document and the product's floating UI (palette, popover, suggestion) above it
world.light: The document lifts one step on the accept or the run; the selection tint is the only colour field.
world.light_build: exposure-plate method on the run (a lift of 0.12 over 0.6 s); selection tint as a plain rect.
world.texture: clean

palettes.notes: the product's light theme; the accent is the selection and the caret
the product's dark theme, tinted away from the stock blue-grey

type_options.sans: the product's own UI sans with its mono
type_options.notes: typed copy at line size inside the document

type_options.sans: a neutral grotesk with a mono partner
type_options.notes: when the product has no type of its own

camera.animator: The edit: select, retype, insert, delete; the camera punches in on the caret at each interaction and falls into the last full stop.
camera.in_shot: A held document with a creep toward the caret.
camera.between: Punch-in inserts on the same render; a cut on the key press; the full-stop dive into the next scene.

cuts.grammar: Cuts on sound: hard cuts on key presses and clicks; edits inside a shot are carried; the dive is one carried move.
cuts.on_sound: The press that triggers each cut is the sound; typing at the house rate with sparse ticks; the dive rises on a long tone.

type.scale_contrast: The product's own strings at ui size, framed large by the punch-in, against one display line typed into the document; the full stop at x20.
type.behaviour: Copy is typed into the product as real input at the house rate (30 characters a second) with bursts and pauses; a line is edited (backspace and retype), never swapped.

signature.name: The full-stop dive
signature.shot: The last line of copy is typed and ends on a full stop. The camera zooms into that full stop at a constant ratio, x20 over 1.4 s (1.036 per frame at 60 fps, so the speed feels even), until the glyph is a disc of ink about 260 px wide; the disc opens as an iris to the far corner in 18 f onto the process the line started, already running at true scale.
signature.build: The document as live DOM text (never a scaled raster); the zoom one transform with scale = 20^t about the full stop's centre, measured once at build time; Iris in rate mode from that centre (irisRadius to farCorner) over the running scene; the process is its own state function, so it opens mid-run.

signature_alt.name: The select-and-retype
signature_alt.shot: A finished line is selected by an I-beam drag (the highlight grows glyph by glyph), holds a beat, and on one frame the selection becomes a caret that types the next line in its place, the camera punching in x2.5 as the first key lands.
signature_alt.build: TypeOn for the typing, a highlight box snapped to glyph edges from measured widths, Cursor with the I-beam; the punch-in a hard cut to a 2.5x framing of the same render.

lockup.shot: Back in the document, the caret types the name on a fresh line at the house rate; the mark sits at the start of the line like an icon; the caret blinks twice and stops.
lockup.build: TypeOn for the name; the supplied logo as an inline SVG glyph; Cursor hidden after the last key.

directions.name: Diorama
directions.idea: The product's process is built as a miniature line under one key light, and the film follows one unit through it.

story.line: One unit enters the model at the left and leaves at the right finished; every station on the way is something the product does to it.

world.set: A tabletop miniature seen from 35 degrees above with a long lens: the product's process as 4-6 stations built from simple extruded blocks (a sorter, a press, a gate, a shelf), one unit (an order, a file, a build) travelling between them on a track. The top and bottom 18 % of the frame fall out of focus like a macro lens on a model.
world.planes: 4: the soft near band, the track and stations, the unit, the soft far band
world.light: One key at 30 degrees from the left: crisp shadows under every block, the unit's shadow riding with it; stations that act lift their top faces +0.06 L for 8 f.
world.light_build: relief method: the set and the unit as SVG blocks, one shadow path per frame; near and far bands are two baked softened stills of the static set.
world.texture: the model's matte material as one static grain plate at 2 %

palettes.notes: a mid stone model; the unit carries the accent once it is finished
a slate model; stations in two lighter steps

camera.between: The camera lets the unit run ahead 0.4 s and catches up with a carried move at the next station.

cuts.grammar: Carried: lateral velocity runs through every station; one hard cut to the overview crane.
cuts.on_sound: Each station acts on a beat with one small mechanical sound; travel is carried by the music.
